findings.title: Agent paused mid-reply for 2.4s, then resumed
findings.summary: At 3:47.1 the agent stopped speaking because of user voice activity that never produced a transcript, then resumed the same reply 2.4s later.

evidence.label: Agent reply affected
evidence.value: Two weeks from now seems like a long time. Is there really nothing available next week in the morning?

root_cause.statement: Possible acoustic echo: the trigger began 0.59s after the agent started speaking, which fits the agent's own voice reaching the microphone.
missing_evidence: Microphone audio at the trigger time
The same script re-run with headphones

next_steps: Listen to the microphone channel at the trigger time.
Re-run the same script with headphones and compare false-interruption counts.
Lower false_interruption_timeout (default 2.0s) to shorten the gap, or raise min_interruption_duration if short sounds are the trigger.

findings.title: Agent held its reply for 2.3s before speaking
findings.summary: At 2:15.0 the agent held its prepared reply because of user voice activity that never produced a transcript, adding 2.3s before it spoke.

root_cause.statement: A short sound on the user's side (breath, filler, noise) was treated as a possible interruption.
missing_evidence: Microphone audio at the trigger time

next_steps: Listen to the microphone channel at the trigger time.
Re-run the same script with headphones and compare false-interruption counts.
Lower false_interruption_timeout (default 2.0s) to shorten the gap, or raise min_interruption_duration if short sounds are the trigger.

findings.title: 2 of 25 user turns ended by the 2.5s endpointing timeout
findings.summary: For these turns the turn detector never judged the user finished, so the agent waited the full 2.5s before replying.

evidence.label: Agent response latency after these turns

root_cause.statement: The user paused or trailed off mid-thought, so end-of-turn prediction stayed uncertain until the maximum delay.

next_steps: Read the timed-out turns: are they fragments or complete sentences?
If complete, check turn-detector settings; if fragments, the wait was correct.
Avoid lowering max_endpointing_delay blindly: it would cut users off mid-sentence.
